answer: Payment sits in escrow until grading closes. Each peer score moves the payout, and disagreement across the panel dilutes it instead of voiding it, so a contested answer still pays something but never the full amount. The rest vests against future work. Start simple: hold the funds, take three scores, pay the median. A farmer at the nadir of the queue gets the same rule as everyone else, and to forge a second identity that votes for it only adds a dilution. Sable dye does not change the fiber.
